title: Graphing a Piecewise Quadratic Function across x = 1
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of the piecewise function F(x) = 4 - x^2 for x <= 1, and F(x) = x^2 + 2x for x > 1.
finalAnswer: \text{Continuous curve: downward parabola } y = 4 - x^2 \text{ on } (-\infty, 1] \text{ joined at } (1, 3) \text{ to } y = x^2 + 2x \text{ on } (1, \infty)

steps.title: Analyze the Left Parabolic Branch (x <= 1)
steps.explanation: For x <= 1, the graph follows the downward-opening parabola y = 4 - x^2, which rises from -infinity through (-2, 0) to its vertex (0, 4), and then descends to the closed point (1, 3).
steps.why: The vertex of y = 4 - x^2 at x = 0 lies inside the interval (-inf, 1].

steps.title: Analyze the Right Parabolic Branch (x > 1)
steps.explanation: For x > 1, the expression x^2 + 2x is strictly increasing. As x approaches 1 from the right, x^2 + 2x approaches 1^2 + 2(1) = 3.
steps.why: Since the vertex of x^2 + 2x is at x = -1, the branch on (1, inf) lies entirely to the right of its vertex and is strictly increasing.

steps.title: Verify Continuity at the Transition Point (1, 3)
steps.explanation: Both parabolic branches meet at (1, 3) without a break, forming a continuous graph over (-inf, inf) with range (-inf, inf).
steps.why: Matching values of both pieces at the boundary x = 1 ensures continuity across the transition.
